branches.conclusion: The central doctoral overview distinguishes NISys provision from cooperative doctorates with partner universities. A separate business doctoral route and its exact award or Operations field mapping have not been established.

NISys provides an academic Dr.-Ing. route with TH Würzburg-Schweinfurt as the title-awarding partner and primary supervision normally by TH Aschaffenburg. The expanded Production and Materials area concerns resource-efficient production processes, lasers/additive manufacturing, automation, functional materials, microsystems and recycling; the Mobility area lists transport technologies and concepts. Those descriptions do not yet establish a substantive Operations or Industrial Engineering doctoral research field. Wider cooperative doctoral field mapping remains unexamined.

sources.note: Read the complete central doctoral overview, NISys versus cooperative routes, doctoral thesis publication and research support. The support college iDok is not treated as a separate degree.

Read the complete NISys page, professor research-topic list, expanded Production and Materials and Mobility areas, and exact doctoral title/awarder FAQ. Dr.-Ing. is explicit; TH Würzburg-Schweinfurt is explicitly title-awarding, with TH AB supervisors. Original German title is preserved. Some display text was subsequently translated into English.

limitations: No qualifying route is added from physical manufacturing, automation or a supervisor’s Industrial Engineering label alone. Exact substantive Operations doctoral field mapping remains unresolved.
Cooperative doctorate possibilities and the partner-led NISys award are distinct from a standalone TH Aschaffenburg PhD. Partner universities are not merged.
